A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FactCheXcker research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, revised and added content.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of FactCheXcker across 11 report-generation models, component evaluations, measurement-error analyses and case studies, including additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds external-dataset results, subgroup analyses, component and activation ablations, and a radiologist review of failure cases.

M1.justification: The described query-code-update pipeline, tool API, GPT-4o mini usage, detector/localizer components and 3–7 cm placement rule remain unchanged. The new MedKLIP and all-reports experiments test alternatives; the selected pipeline retains ImageNet pretraining and report-triggered processing.

E1.justification: Appendix E adds evaluation on the CheXpert Plus (Stanford-CXR) test set, extending the full-pipeline evaluation beyond MIMIC-CXR to another institution. The ETT tasks remain unchanged. The external measurement comparison is limited to 4–18 overlapping reports per model.

E2.justification: The same 11 report-generation comparators remain. New Table 9 evaluates a MedKLIP-pretrained detector against the retained ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50+ module, adding a focused component comparator.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds an all-reports activation control and evaluation stratified by sex, age, comparison-study availability and clinical indication. The stated primary MIMIC-CXR splits, annotation procedure and metrics remain unchanged; the revised primary scores do not themselves establish a protocol change.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands analysis beyond the retained error distributions and failure-rate plots. It adds subgroup analysis, a pretraining ablation, an all-reports activation experiment and manual review of 20 failures. Figure 5 retains one success example and replaces the other with four failure examples.

E5.justification: Both versions use Figure 3 significance markers with p < 0.1 and report measurement-error standard deviation in Table 2. No new repeated-run, seed, confidence-interval or statistical-testing procedure is documented; changed values and significance outcomes are result changes.

E6.justification: Core results change throughout Tables 2 and 4–6 and Figures 3–4. Table 4 replaces average original/FactCheXcker MAE values of 2.48/1.28 with 1.93/0.82. RadFM changes from improving, 1.69 to 1.10, to worsening, 0.65 to 1.04. Appendix E and the failure audit add substantial new outcomes. These are revised reported results, without an explained basis for attributing differences to improved methodology.

T1.justification: The Composite = MAE/F1 definition and placement thresholds are retained, with no new proofs or derivations. The added verbal hallucination definition in Section 3.1 restates the existing object-versus-measurement distinction.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction raise the headline claimed average MAE improvement from 94% to 135%. The framework contribution, ETT focus and claim of improving all 11 models otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 adds specific failure explanations involving tube misidentification, obscured carina landmarks and image rotation, and identifies a need for training on multiple-tube cases. Section 5.2 now reports the all-reports precision tradeoff previously discussed hypothetically. Appendix E acknowledges the small external ETT sample.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract and a Section 3 footnote. The appendix prompt templates, API documentation and CarinaNet fine-tuning details are retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography retains the same works. Section 2 expands the approach's positioning around requiring no model-weight access and using locally deployable tools in resource-limited or privacy-centered hospitals.

P1.justification: Localized edits simplify related-work and method prose, replace symbolic module names, rename Section 5.5 to Discussion and relabel the appendix as Supplementary Material. Author-contribution and acknowledgment text also changes. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is substantially redesigned into a retained successful workflow beside four failure illustrations. Tables 7–10 add displays for the new robustness experiments. Figure 1 labels, existing table-row ordering and supplementary prompt/API formatting also change.

improvement.justification: External validation, ablations, failure analysis and code-access information strengthen evidence and transparency. However, unexplained core-score revisions introduce material inconsistencies: Section 5.3 still claims every model improves despite RadFM worsening in Table 4, while Section 5.2 replaces the correct 625% precision improvement with 1024% despite unchanged values of 0.08 and 0.58. These benefits and reporting harms prevent a reliable net-quality judgment from the PDFs.
